Frequently asked questions

Which regulations do these courses follow?
  • OSHA Benzene Awareness Training: in accordance with Federal OSHA Regulations 29 CFR 1910.1028 and 29 CFR 1926.1128.
  • OSHA Cadmium Awareness Training: in accordance with Federal OSHA Regulations 29 CFR 1910.1027 and 29 CFR 1926.1127.
  • OSHA Hexavalent Chromium Awareness Training: in accordance with Federal OSHA Regulations 29 CFR 1910 Subpart Z, 1910.1026 and 29 CFR 1926 Subpart Z, 1926.1126.
  • OSHA Silica Awareness Training: in accordance with Federal OSHA Regulations 29 CFR 1910.1053 and 29 CFR 1926.1153.
  • OSHA Asbestos Awareness Training: in accordance with Federal OSHA Regulations 29 CFR 1910.1001 and 29 CFR 1926.1101.
  • OSHA Lead Awareness Training: in accordance with Federal OSHA Regulations 29 CFR 1926.62.
  • OSHA Hexavalent Chromium Safety and Remediation Training: in accordance with Federal OSHA Regulations 29 CFR 1910.1026 and 29 CFR 1926.1126.
  • OSHA Competent Person for Silica Training: in accordance with Federal OSHA Regulations 29 CFR 1926.1153.
How long does Silica, Lead, Asbestos & Hexavalent Chromium Training take?
  • OSHA Benzene Awareness Training: 1 hour.
  • OSHA Cadmium Awareness Training: 1 hour.
  • OSHA Hexavalent Chromium Awareness Training: 2 hours.
  • OSHA Silica Awareness Training: 2 hours.
  • Dust Disturbance and Mitigation Awareness Training: 1 hour.
  • OSHA Asbestos Awareness Training: 3 hours.
  • OSHA Lead Awareness Training: 3 hours.
  • OSHA Hexavalent Chromium Safety and Remediation Training: 6 hours.
  • OSHA Competent Person for Silica Training: 8 hours.

Training is self-paced, so you can stop and pick up where you left off at any time.

You get a 3-month completion timeline, 1-year access to training materials.

Yes. You can download your certificate of completion as soon as you pass the final exam.
